content.text:
Home's printer cards now update live while Home is on screen, with no leaving and coming back. All three checks passed: the new `--home-live` harness mode (62 checks, 0 failures), `--printer-setup`, and the default full shell scenario. Nothing is committed; the changes are in this worktree for you to review.

I based it on `jusprin-newui`, which already contains the printer-card-messaging branch's commits. `home_card()` isn't committed anywhere; it's only uncommitted work in the printer-card-messaging worktree, which I left alone. My change compares the serialized JSON rather than `PrinterEntry` fields, so it doesn't depend on the card shape that work is changing.

## Upstream events: none to bind to
- **Device pushes:** OrcaSlicer fires no event. The cloud and LAN message handlers in `GUI_App` parse the message and then call the Sidebar directly through `Plater::update_machine_sync_status()`. Adding an event there would mean editing a busy upstream file in two places.
- **The Monitor:** it stays current by polling. A 1000 ms timer re-reads the device list (`Monitor.cpp`, `REFRESH_INTERVAL`).
- **The header status row and spool chip:** they only react to project, slice and ledger events and to the spool menu's `store_changed`. The header is hidden on Home, so it has nothing to reuse.
- **Offline:** this is time passing (the 30 s freshness window), not a message, so a timer is needed anyway.

## Chosen trigger: one 1 s tick, sent only on change
- **Where:** `HomeWebView::set_live()` runs a 1 s timer, the Monitor's own rate. The shell turns it on and off as Home is selected. A tick does nothing while the printer conversation covers the page or the window is minimized.
- **What a tick does:** `HomeHost::refresh_if_changed()` re-reads only the printers, serializes them the way the page receives them, and compares that with what was last sent. It sends the full `state` only when a card would look different.
- **Coverage:** the tick covers every source in the brief, because `printers()` reads all of them: device updates, the Offline transition, print-host changes, profile changes and spool-store changes. There are no separate hooks.
- **Upstream files touched:** none. Everything is in fork-owned files, so no rebase simulation was needed.
- **Not disturbing the page:** the page keeps each card mounted, so an open menu, a half-typed rename and scroll position survive a push. I covered menus and renames with new page tests and the menu with the harness. An added printer's place at the top and its highlight now carry across live pushes. Before, any later push put the column back in alphabetical order and cut the glow short.

## Cost
- **Tick with nothing changed:** about 35 µs, averaged over 500 calls in the app. Nothing is sent. That is roughly 0.004% of the UI thread.
- **Tick with a change:** a full state, including projects. During a real print that's about once a minute, because the "Xm left" text changes, plus once per percent of progress. I did not measure the cost of a send with a full gallery of thumbnails, because the test fixture has no recent projects.

## Verification
- **`--home-live`** (new): saves and connects the fake Bambu printer, then reads the card from the Home page itself, never from the backend. Home is never left and refreshed only once, on the way in.
  - Online, then Printing at 43%, then Offline all arrived live. Offline showed 31 s after the fake went silent (the 30 s window plus one tick).
  - A card menu opened first stayed open through both changes.
  - Over 4 s of unchanged status pushes, 0 messages were sent. Once Home was hidden, nothing was sent at all.
- **Unit tests:** `jusprin_tests "[home]"` all pass, including 3 new ones (27 cases). The Home page tests pass 49/49, including 2 new ones.
- **Regression:** `--printer-setup` and the default scenario both pass with 0 failures.

The first harness run failed at Offline because of a mistake in my check, not in the feature. On this branch the offline card's Reconnect button uses the same `launch-monitor` style as Launch monitor, so the check now matches buttons by their label.

The changes are in `HomeHost`, `HomeWebView`, `ShellController::on_page_changed`, `tests/jusprin/test_home_host.cpp`, `HomeUI/src/App.test.tsx` and the `--home-live` mode in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`. The build tree is `C:\b\hlv`.

**What happened**

Home's printer cards used to freeze until you left Home and came back. Now they update on their own while you're looking at Home. If a printer starts printing, its progress moves, it drops offline, or its spools or settings change, the card catches up within about a second.

- **How it works:** OrcaSlicer doesn't announce when a printer reports in, so there was nothing to listen for. Home now checks its printer cards once a second, the same rate OrcaSlicer's own Monitor screen uses. It only redraws the page when a card would actually look different. A check with nothing new costs about 35 millionths of a second. The checking stops whenever Home isn't on screen.
- **Nothing on screen gets disrupted:** an open card menu, a half-typed rename and your scroll position all survive an update. A just-added printer keeps its place at the top and its highlight.
- **No OrcaSlicer files were changed**, only JusPrin's own code, so this adds no rebase burden.

- **New automated test:** it drives the fake Bambu printer through Idle, Printing and Offline while Home stays open. It reads what the page itself displays, not just the data behind it. All three states showed up. Offline appeared 31 seconds after the printer went quiet, which is the expected 30 plus one check.
- **Existing tests:** they all still pass.
- **One stumble, since fixed:** my first test run failed at the Offline step. The cause was my test, not the feature: on the offline card, Reconnect shares a style with the Launch monitor button, so the test couldn't tell them apart.

**What I need from you**

Only a decision: should I commit this and open a pull request? Per the project rules I haven't committed anything; the changes are in this session's working folder.
